correctness.rationale: For normalized unweighted ball monomials, the radial primitive maps each basis vector to a distinct shifted basis vector with the explicitly calculated weight. This exactly diagonalizes T*T. Fixing the transverse index gives a weighted degree multiplicity binomial(M+h-1,h-1), and the tail is asymptotic to A_beta M^(-k/2). The uniform upper bound A_beta/(M+1)^(k/2) justifies dominated convergence over all transverse indices; strict damping makes the dominating series summable. Counting asymptotic inversion and harmonic sums give all assertions, including the sharp ideal endpoint. The finite checker independently tests the normalization identities on 40065 exact rational assertions; it is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The invariant is the natural singular-value counting function of boundary-contact companion operators, not an arbitrary finite slice. The model systematically varies the dimension of contact, the transverse vanishing order, and every strict contraction, including full-rank maps outside the source compact-range case. An exact coefficient and critical weak-Schatten/logarithmic trace law sharpen qualitative compactness/ideal membership and reveal the dimension/order phase transition p=2h/k independent of the number of damped directions. The parameter-dependent series interpolates toward the rank-deficient projection benchmark.
